description: AFTERLIFE is an independently developed project by Insha Nishad, created as part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. I independently researched, designed, and developed an interactive webpage exploring forgotten space missions and the discoveries left behind by spacecraft, rovers, and other explorers.
summary:
AFTERLIFE is an interactive educational webpage that explores the stories of spacecraft, rovers and scientific equipment that have been left behind after their missions. It takes visitors on a journey across three destinations: the Moon, Mars and Deep Space.

Through interactive profiles, short mission stories, interesting discoveries and a final quiz, the project introduces visitors to lesser-known space explorers. It explains what happened to them after their missions ended.

The project aims to make space exploration more accessible and engaging, particularly for younger audiences, while highlighting how past missions continue to contribute to our understanding of the universe.
details:
AFTERLIFE is an interactive educational webpage that takes visitors on a journey through the Moon, Mars and Deep Space, introducing them to spacecraft, rovers and scientific equipment whose missions have ended or whose signals have gone silent.

The webpage is organized into different destinations, each featuring interactive elements that reveal the stories, discoveries and final journeys of lesser-known space explorers. It also includes interesting facts and a final quiz to help visitors test what they have learned.

I aim to make space exploration more engaging and accessible, particularly for younger audiences. Rather than focusing only on famous astronauts and major missions, AFTERLIFE highlights the machines that explored beyond Earth and the discoveries they left behind. Through this project, I hope to encourage curiosity, appreciation for scientific progress, and a deeper interest in space exploration.

The creative aspect of my project lies in its storytelling approach. Instead of presenting information as a collection of facts, I have turned completed space missions into stories that visitors can explore at their own pace through interactive elements and visual content.

While developing the project, I considered the intended audience, ease of navigation, accuracy of scientific information, and the amount of content displayed on each page. I aimed to keep the information concise and understandable without losing the significance of each mission.

Tools and software: Genially and NASA's publicly available mission information and resources.
